title: manifest push: push error discarded when `--digestfile` is used, exits 0
body:
### Issue Description

`buildah manifest push --digestfile` writes an empty digest file and exits `0` when the push fails.

Two separate problems in `manifestPush()` in [`cmd/buildah/manifest.go`](https://github.com/containers/buildah/blob/v1.45.1/cmd/buildah/manifest.go#L1230-L1242) combine to produce this:

```go
_, digest, err := list.Push(getContext(), dest, options)

if err == nil && opts.rm {
	_, err = store.DeleteImage(manifestList.ID(), true)
}

if opts.digestfile != "" {
	if err = os.WriteFile(opts.digestfile, []byte(digest.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
		return util.GetFailureCause(err, fmt.Errorf("failed to write digest to file %q: %w", opts.digestfile, err))
	}
}

return err
```

1. The `opts.digestfile` block is not guarded by `err == nil`, so it runs even when `list.Push` failed. On the failure path `digest` is the zero value, and since `digest.Digest` is a `string` type whose `String()` is a plain cast, `digest.String()` returns `""` an empty file is written.

2. `if err = os.WriteFile(...)` *assigns to the existing* `err` rather than declaring a new one. When `WriteFile` succeeds it overwrites the push error with `nil`, so the closing `return err` returns `nil` and the command exits successfully.

The second point is the more serious one: the push error is swallowed entirely, so the failure is invisible to any caller checking the exit code.

Note that `buildah push` does **not** have this bug. In [`cmd/buildah/push.go`](https://github.com/containers/buildah/blob/v1.45.1/cmd/buildah/push.go#L262) the error path returns early, so the digestfile is only written after a successful push. Only `manifest push` is affected.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a manifest list with at least one image:

```console
$ buildah manifest create example
$ buildah build --manifest example --platform linux/amd64 -t example .
```

2. Push it to a destination that will fail, e.g. a registry you are not authenticated against, or one that does not exist:

```console
$ buildah manifest push --all --digestfile /tmp/digest example docker://registry.invalid/nonexistent/repo
$ echo "exit status: $?"
$ ls -l /tmp/digest
$ wc -c /tmp/digest
```

### Describe the results you received

The push fails, but the exit status is `0` and `/tmp/digest` exists with a size of 0 bytes. No error is reported from the push itself.

```console
exit status: 0
-rw-r--r--. 1 user user 0 ... /tmp/digest
0 /tmp/digest
```

### Describe the results you expected

A non-zero exit status and the push error propagated to the caller. The digest file should not be created or written at all when the push fails, a caller should never observe an empty digest file.

### buildah version output

```console
(verified by code inspection against tag v1.45.1 and main at 596ece93bbb07d15c53c5b044a08326c4a72acce; the affected code is identical in both)
```

### buildah info output

I'm running this from a CI pipeline, that only outputs `buildah version`
```console
Version:         1.43.1
Go Version:      go1.26.1-X:nodwarf5
Image Spec:      1.1.1
Runtime Spec:    1.2.1
CNI Spec:        1.1.0
libcni Version:  
image Version:   5.39.2
Git Commit:      
Built:           Wed Apr  8 19:37:51 2026
OS/Arch:         linux/arm64
BuildPlatform:   linux/arm64/v8
```

### Provide your storage.conf

```console
[storage]
      driver = "vfs"
      graphRoot = "${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/.buildah-storage"
      runRoot = "/tmp/buildah-run"
```

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Encountered in CI (GitLab CI) using the `quay.io/buildah/stable` image. The practical impact is that a pipeline step doing `buildah manifest push --digestfile ...` succeeds despite pushing nothing, and a later step that reads the digest file gets an empty value. In our case the next step signs the pushed image with cosign, so a failed push silently turned into a green pipeline with an unsigned (and nonexistent) image. We now have to defensively check that the digest file is both present and non-empty.

### Additional information

A minimal fix is to guard the write and avoid clobbering `err`:

```go
_, digest, err := list.Push(getContext(), dest, options)
if err != nil {
	return err
}

if opts.rm {
	if _, err := store.DeleteImage(manifestList.ID(), true); err != nil {
		return err
	}
}

if opts.digestfile != "" {
	if err := os.WriteFile(opts.digestfile, []byte(digest.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
		return util.GetFailureCause(err, fmt.Errorf("failed to write digest to file %q: %w", opts.digestfile, err))
	}
}

return nil
```
